faq.q: Can I claim HRA if I pay rent to my parents?
faq.a: Yes, you can, provided there's a genuine landlord-tenant relationship, you actually pay rent, and your parents declare this rental income in their tax returns. Ensure you have proper rent receipts and a rental agreement.

faq.q: What if my owned house is vacant? Can I still claim both?
faq.a: Yes, if your owned house is vacant (not self-occupied) and you are living in rented accommodation, you can claim both HRA exemption and home loan interest deduction. The vacant property would be treated as 'deemed to be let out' for tax purposes, and you can claim the interest deduction.

faq.q: Is there a limit to the total amount I can claim for both HRA and home loan interest?
faq.a: While there isn't a combined overall limit, each deduction has its own specific limits. HRA exemption is based on actual HRA received, rent paid, and salary percentage, while home loan interest for self-occupied property is capped at ₹2 lakhs. For let-out properties, the interest deduction isn't capped, but the loss from house property that can be set off against other income is limited to ₹2 lakhs per year.

faq.q: Do I need to declare my owned property details to my employer for HRA exemption?
faq.a: Generally, no. Your employer primarily needs rent receipts for HRA. However, for home loan interest deduction, you typically submit the interest certificate to your employer for TDS adjustment. It's your responsibility to ensure you meet the conditions for claiming both benefits.

faq.q: What if I own multiple properties?
faq.a: If you own multiple properties, only one can be treated as self-occupied. The others are deemed to be let out for tax purposes, even if they are vacant. You can claim home loan interest deduction on all properties, but the loss from house property that can be set off against other income is capped at ₹2 lakhs per year. HRA exemption rules remain the same for your rented accommodation.

faq.q: Can NRIs claim HRA and home loan benefits?
faq.a: NRIs can claim home loan interest deduction if they have taken a loan for a property in India, subject to the same conditions as residents. However, HRA exemption is typically for salaried individuals receiving HRA in India for rent paid in India. If an NRI is earning salary income in India and receiving HRA, they can claim it.

fact_check.summary: The article provides largely accurate information regarding claiming both HRA and home loan interest deductions under the Indian Income Tax Act, outlining specific scenarios and necessary documentation. However, there are some inaccuracies regarding the classification of metro cities for HRA calculation and the treatment of vacant properties.

corrections.note: Corrected the clarification regarding Bengaluru's metro status for HRA calculation and refined the explanation of 'deemed to be let out' for vacant properties.

edits.why: The original statement was too broad. Only properties beyond the first two self-occupied ones are 'deemed to be let out' if vacant. The correction clarifies that the first two vacant properties can still be treated as self-occupied.
